title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving assistance for wash to the most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas in Dinsor district, Bay region

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtDiinsoor has experienced acute climatic stress since late 2020. The failed Deyr 2024 and projected poor Gu 2025 rains have led to rainfall deficits of 45–60% across Bay Region, severely depleting water sources like shallow wells and surface catchments (berkads) (FAO, 2025 ACAPS, 2025). Seasonal outlooks emphasize significant risks to water and food security, with drought conditions expected to worsen in the coming season (FAO, 2025). The prolonged drought has devastated agro-pastoral livelihoods in Bay Region. According to IPC, 3.4 million people already face crisis or worse food security (IPC 3+), projected to rise to 4.4 million by June 2025 (UNICEF/FAO, 2025). Conflict is compounding the crisis: Bay Region—including Diinsoor—is among the worst affected, with inter-clan violence and armed group activities driving conflict-related displacement (Informer East Africa, 2025 ACAPS, 2025). Over 477,000 people were newly displaced within Somalia in 2024, with Diinsoor ranking as a conflict displacement hotspot. Recent assessments reveal Diinsoor’s WASH situation has deteriorated. Diinsoor is classified among districts facing severe to extreme WASH stress, with traditional water sources such as shallow wells and berkads frequently drying out (WASH Cluster, 2024). Recent humanitarian bulletins note that shallow wells and boreholes have largely failed, prompting sudden surges in trucked water deliveries—sometimes covering over 50% of water needs. During this Gu 2025 and past Deyr season ( Oct-Nov 2024), rainfall was only 30–45% of average, leading to drying of water points across Bay region and elevated risk of waterborne diseases (HNRP, 2025). The absence of proper latrines not only poses serious public health risks, particularly the spread of cholera and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) but also exposes women and girls to increased protection risks (Protection Cluster, 2024). To address these issues, The project proposes to deliver emergency WASH assistance to drought and conflict-affected communities in Diinsoor through integrated WASH package: (1) Rehabilitation of sustainable water points (one shallow well equipped with solar pumping system and another two shallow wells equipped with hand pumps, serving 3,000 people), backed by water quality monitoring, testing, basic water treatment and establishing and training of three water management committees (2) Construction of gender segregated sanitation infrastructure, including 65 flood-proof latrines and 10 PwD-accessible units benefiting 2250 people including the PwD, supported by distribution of 100 sanitation kits and 33 clean-up campaigns and (3) Hygiene behavior change initiatives including distribution of 2000 hygiene kits, 32 targeted hygiene promotion campaigns and education sessions at communal and facility level. The project will target vulnerable communities at the rural villages and IDPs. The project aims to improve access to safe water sources, sanitation facilities, and hygiene education for vulnerable communities, particularly women, girls, and persons with disabilities. These integrated WASH interventions will provide immediate lifesaving support to 12,000 vulnerable individuals (3361 women, 3120 girls, 2639 men and 2880 boys) mitigate impact of drought and displacement, reduce waterborne disease transmission, and strengthen community resilience against ongoing climatic shocks.ltbrgtlt/pgt
